sources.title: MiniMax M2.5: Built for Real-World Productivity
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The dated February 12 release describes M2.5 as an M2-series model extensively trained with reinforcement learning, without announcing pruning, expert expansion or a new modality. It adds no separate active-count scalar.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 official model card and released weights
sources.evidence: MiniMax publishes the exact model weights, text-generation model card, Transformers deployment and tool-calling guide. Model card license label is modified-mit.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 released configuration
sources.evidence: Freshly read the pinned and current M2.5 configs on October 27; they are identical. Compared with official M2: both have 62 layers, hidden size 3072, expert FFN 1536, 256 experts with top-8 routing, 48 Q/8 KV heads of dimension 128, vocabulary 200064, no shared expert and matching MTP flags. No size-changing configuration difference was found.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 reference implementation
sources.evidence: Causal decoder implements full softmax attention with grouped KV heads, RoPE, QK normalization, and sparse expert MLPs. The router correction bias is registered as a buffer; this alone does not establish its training status. Text token embedding and language-model output head establish text input/output.

sources.title: MiniMax Model License for MiniMax-M2.5
sources.evidence: The distributed license is titled MINIMAX MODEL LICENSE and permits use, redistribution and modification subject to notice, use-policy and other terms; it is not the unmodified MIT license. Its version date is 2026-02-13, later than the February 12 announcement.

sources.title: MiniMax staff statement on M2-series size
sources.evidence: On February 15, ryanlee-dev, visibly identified as a MiniMax organization member, states that all M2-series models have 230B parameters in the exact M2.5 repository. Supports a nominal total; the user-authored title mentions 10B active but the staff reply does not confirm that count.

sources.title: MiniMax M2.5 vLLM deployment guide
sources.evidence: Explicitly applies to M2.5 and states maximum per-sequence context remains 196K; distinguishes aggregate KV-cache capacity from per-sequence context. Config supplies the exact 196608 value.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 Tool Calling Guide
sources.evidence: Explicitly documents M2.5 tool support and structured XML tool-call output, with tool definitions converted to text.

sources.title: The MiniMax-M2 Series: Mini Activations Unleashing Max Real-World Intelligence
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Sections 1 and 9 describe the pretrained M2 backbone and post-training progression through M2.5 to M2.7; section 2 reports 9.8B activated parameters. Combined with matching official M2/M2.5 dimensions and routing, this supports a labeled nominal active-count inference. Table 4 contains exact M2.5 benchmark scores, not a separate active-count column. No pruning, expert expansion or modality change for M2.5 is described.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 checkpoint index and bounded Safetensors headers
sources.evidence: All 125 published shard JSON headers at revision 2515a3ea0afec1dd22d0c7794b3a91557804d195 were read through bounded HTTP ranges and matched all 96103 indexed tensors. There are 228689748992 .weight elements, 15872 routing-bias elements, 13880064 FP8 inverse-scale elements and no other tensor classes. No MTP tensors appear in the release despite MTP config flags. Raw 228703644928 storage elements are not a learned-parameter count.

sources.title: MiniMax native OpenAI-compatible API documentation
sources.evidence: Current supported-model table only lists M3-series models; it no longer independently establishes M2.5 context. The same page still explicitly lists M2.5 in instructions to preserve think content and says M2.x thinking cannot be disabled. Historical 204800-token M2.5 API context was not recovered as a complete primary table during this audit.

sources.title: MiniMax staff clarification about M2.5-Lightning
sources.evidence: MiniMax organization member ryanlee-dev explains that Lightning uses more inference resources and the model parameters remain exactly the same. This clarifies serving variants but does not independently state an activated-parameter count.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2 official base configuration
sources.evidence: Freshly retrieved October 27. Compared with the official M2.5 config: all parameter-bearing hidden/expert/head/layer/vocabulary dimensions and top-8-of-256 routing match, with no shared expert. Confirms unchanged nominal activation geometry for the report’s named post-training progression.

sources.title: Forge: Scalable Agent RL Framework and Algorithm
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The February 13 developer article attributes M2.5 gains to agent-native reinforcement learning and training-inference infrastructure; it describes no pruning, distillation, expert expansion or modality change. Provides training context, not an independent numeric count.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.7 later model card and comparison figure
sources.evidence: Read October 27, including visual inspection of benchmark_overview.png. M2.5 bars report benchmark scores only; no total/active parameter comparison column is present. The series report supplies the count and lineage basis.

sources.title: MiniMax-M3 later model card and comparison table
sources.evidence: Read October 27, including visual inspection of benchmark.jpeg. Its approximately 428B/23B disclosure describes M3; the comparison image reports benchmark results, with no M2.5 activated-parameter column. These later-model counts are not transferred.

sources.title: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash later model card
sources.evidence: Retrieved directly October 27 after the web reader failed. Read its model specifications and complete HTML comparison table: approximately 428B/23B applies to M3.1-Flash; no M2.5 count is supplied. Its documented sparse-attention and draft-head changes concern the separate M3 lineage.

name.note: Exact name used in the original announcement and official checkpoint.

developer.note: MiniMax announces and distributes this model.

family.note: Retains the catalog broad MiniMax family identifier; the developer identifies the exact model as part of its M2 series.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit public release is the dated February 12 announcement, corroborated by the official repository creation on February 12. The license version date February 13 does not move that public release date.

open_weights.note: Official FP8 weights are publicly distributed in 125 Safetensors shards.

license.note: Actual distributed license title. Model-card metadata still labels it modified-mit, but the distributed agreement contains its own notice and prohibited-use terms; this is not plain MIT. Hosted API terms are separate.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit reconfirms the developer’s nominal 230B total for all M2-series models, stated by MiniMax staff in the M2.5 repository. Preserve this published precision; neither the earlier tensor census nor the base report’s 229.9B is substituted as an exact M2.5 total.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 9.8B activated per token, inferred from the developer’s explicit M2-backbone post-training progression through M2.5 and the freshly matched M2/M2.5 configuration dimensions and top-8-of-256 routing. No size-changing training or modality change is described. This follows the report’s main-model activation convention, not a new exact tensor sum or total-equals-active assumption. Later first-party comparisons add no conflicting exact-M2.5 active count.

architecture.note: Decoder-only Transformer MoE: 62 layers, 256 routed experts with 8 selected per token, full grouped-query softmax attention (48 Q heads, 8 KV heads), RoPE and QK normalization. Exact code does not implement Lightning Attention.

context_window.note: Released checkpoint limit from exact configuration, corroborated by developer deployment guide. Replaces baseline 204800 because a complete historical native-API table for that number was not recovered. This is a checkpoint specification, not a claim about current or historical hosted endpoint limits.

modalities.note: Text-generation checkpoint consumes token IDs and emits vocabulary logits; reference code has no visual/audio encoder. Office workflows use external tools and do not establish native document, image or audio modalities.

reasoning.note: Release explicitly describes efficient reasoning; later report evaluates exact M2.5 with thinking enabled and API docs retain its think-content requirements.

tool_call.note: Developer provides exact-model tool-calling support and XML output protocol.

description.value: Open-weight MiniMax M2-series language model trained with reinforcement learning for coding, tool use, search, and office workflows.
description.note: Replaces time-dependent prior-model wording with a factual scope summary grounded in release and deployment material.

patch.notes: 230B is the developer’s nominal total. The 9.8B active count is a nominal inference from the documented M2 post-training lineage and matching backbone dimensions/routing, following the report’s main-model convention. Context 196608 is the released checkpoint limit; historical 204800-token native API context was not independently recovered. Current license is the custom MiniMax Model License, despite the model card metadata label modified-mit.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains developer nominal 230B total and recovers 9.8B active as an explicit nominal lineage inference. The later M2-series report describes the sized base and post-training progression through M2.5; fresh official configurations confirm matching dimensions and routing. Original release, Forge training details and later comparison cards reveal no conflicting structural change or active count. All unrelated assessments and prior checkpoint/context/license qualifications are preserved; no weight shards were downloaded.
